title: The Job Abroad
intro: An agent offers a well-paid job abroad, with a visa and flights included. Almost.
Tap anything that looks odd to sniff it closer. Pin what is suspicious, clear what is harmless.
When you are sure, decide what to do.

notify.text: Job abroad: free visa, high salary

screen.context: You are looking for work abroad.

msg.text: No papers to check, we handle everything.

job.label: A huge salary for easy work
job.why: Big pay for little skill is the bait.

visa.label: "Free visa"
visa.lens: A visa is not something an agent can promise.
visa.why: Check what the destination country's own official site says.

fee.label: A big agent fee up front
fee.why: Honest placement firms are paid by the employer, not you.

third.label: Fly to a third country first
third.lens: You are asked to fly somewhere else and wait.
third.why: This is how people get stranded.

noreg.label: "No papers to check"
noreg.lens: They give no registration or licence number.
noreg.why: A real agent shows a licence you can check.

num.label: A mobile number
num.lens: No office address, only a mobile.

actions.label: Check the agent's licence on the official government list
Report the number and delete it

block_report.line: Reported and deleted. Your phone company can block the number.

verify.line: The official list had no agent by that name, and the government warned about fake job agents. Case cracked.

ignore.line: You stayed safe. But the same scam is still landing on other people.

go_ahead.line: The $1,600 was lost. The "visa" never came, and the agent's number went dead.

what_if.go_ahead: Checking the agent on the official list would have ended it. A real agent is licensed and does not ask this much in advance.
what_if.ignore: Reporting takes two taps and helps protect other people.
what_if.verify: Checking was smart. Reporting it as well helps protect other people.

golden_rule: A job abroad with a huge salary and a big agent fee is a scam. Check the agent on the official list first.

quick_check.q: An agent offers a job abroad at $4,000 a month, asks $1,600 first and says you will fly to a third country. What do you do?

options.text: Check the agent on the official government list. Do not pay

quick_check.explain: A huge fee and a third country are classic signs.

hints.nudge: Would an employer ask you to pay and to fly somewhere else?

rows.v: Look the agent up on the official list
